title: Ambiguous or incomplete source
scenario: A draft architecture proposal for a product-analytics event pipeline that contradicts itself (hourly batches vs real time; 30 vs 90 days raw retention), leaves gaps (registry owner, aggregate retention, rejected events, cost) and states one relationship vaguely (enrichment 'uses' the user service). The canvas must show the stated design, keep conflicts and unknowns visible and apart, and invent nothing.
audience: Engineers and a tech lead reviewing the proposal before approving phase 1
objective: See what the proposal actually commits to, and exactly which points are contradictory or missing, without the canvas silently picking a side or filling a gap.

units.quote: The growth team wants to understand how customers use the Lumen web and mobile apps.
Today, product events are scattered across three logging tools, and nobody can answer a simple funnel question without exporting CSV files by hand.
This proposal describes a single pipeline that collects product-analytics events, enriches them and makes them available in the warehouse.
The first questions the team wants answered are how many new accounts finish onboarding, and which features paying customers use in their first month.
Client SDKs in the web and mobile apps send events to a collector service over HTTPS.
Clients batch events and send them every 10 seconds, or sooner when the app goes to the background.
Each event carries an event name, a timestamp, an anonymous device id and, for signed-in users, an account id.
The collector validates each event against the schema registry and rejects events that do not match a registered schema.

critical.note: Validation against the registry is the pipeline's only quality gate.

units.quote: Accepted events are published to the `analytics.events` topic on the message bus.
An enrichment step consumes the topic and adds account attributes, such as plan tier and region.
The enrichment step uses the user service.

critical.note: 'Uses' doesn't say whether enrichment calls the service per event, caches lookups or reads a replica; that choice changes load and failure modes.

ambiguity.note: The kind of dependency is not stated. u15 (keep the user service lightly loaded) argues against a call per event but does not settle it.

units.quote: If an account cannot be found, the event is passed on without account attributes.
Enriched events are then written to the warehouse in hourly batches, where the analytics team builds dashboards on them.

ambiguity.note: Write cadence: hourly batches here, real time in the Freshness section.

units.quote: The first dashboards will cover the onboarding funnel and weekly active accounts per plan tier.
We expect the user service to stay lightly loaded, so enrichment should avoid adding much traffic to it.
Every event type must be registered before clients can send it.

critical.note: No unregistered event type is accepted.

units.quote: Schemas are versioned, and a breaking change requires a new version rather than an edit to the existing one.
Ownership of the schema registry has not been decided; the platform team and the data team have each suggested the other.

critical.note: No owner: must not be filled in with either team.

units.quote: Product managers have asked to see feature adoption as it happens, especially during launches.
Launch reviews usually happen within 2 hours of a release.
With this pipeline, events reach the warehouse in real time, so launch dashboards stay current.

critical.note: 'In real time' contradicts hourly batches (u13); with hourly batches a launch review 2 hours in sees at most two loads.

ambiguity.note: Freshness claim inconsistent with the design section.

units.quote: Raw events will be kept for 30 days and then deleted; only aggregated tables are kept longer.

critical.note: 30 days here, 90 days in the components table (u32).

ambiguity.note: Raw-event retention differs between text and table.

units.quote: Deleting raw events after a fixed period also limits what an access request has to search.
How long the aggregated tables are kept is TBD.
Events must not contain email addresses or free-text input from users.
IP addresses are truncated by the collector before an event is published.
This pipeline is not meant for operational monitoring or alerting; error logs and service metrics stay in the existing observability stack.
It will not replace the billing system's records of revenue.
| Collector | Platform team | none |
| `analytics.events` topic | Platform team | 7 days |
| Enrichment | Data team | none |
| Warehouse raw events | Data team | 90 days |

critical.note: 90 days here, 30 days in the retention section (u22).

ambiguity.note: Raw-event retention differs between text and table.

units.quote: | Schema registry | TBD | indefinite |
Phase 1 covers the web app's sign-up and checkout events.
Phase 2 adds mobile events once the mobile SDK is ready; no date has been set for it.
Phase 1 is expected to take about 6 weeks for 2 engineers.
The cost of running the pipeline has not been estimated yet.

critical.note: Missing estimate; must not be invented.

units.quote: Who owns the schema registry?
What happens to events the collector rejects: are they dropped, or kept somewhere for debugging?

critical.note: The only statement about rejected events; it is a question, not a design.

units.quote: Should mobile events use the same schemas as web events?
We ask for approval to start phase 1 while the open questions are settled in parallel.

safeToOmit.why: The open-questions list repeats the registry-ownership gap already stated in u18.

provenance.note: Original text written for this dataset. Lumen, the team names, the topic name, every figure (10 seconds, 2 hours, 30 and 90 days, 7 days, 6 weeks) and the contradictions themselves are invented on purpose to exercise conflicting and missing information.
